recent_posts.title: Tails 7.7.2
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.7.2 is an emergency release addressing a critical Linux kernel security vulnerability called 'Copy Fail'. The flaw could allow an application running inside Tails to gain administration privileges, potentially enabling an attacker to take full control of the system and deanonymize the user. The Linux kernel has been updated to version 6.12.85 to patch this issue. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later, and manual upgrade instructions are provided for cases where automatic upgrades fail.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.7.1
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.7.1 is an emergency release addressing important security vulnerabilities in Tor Browser. It updates Tor Browser to 15.0.11 (fixing several Firefox 140.10.1 vulnerabilities), updates Thunderbird to 140.10.0, and removes the ability to boot ISO images from USB sticks. The ISO change saves space and prevents confusion, as USB images have been the recommended installation method since 2019. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.7
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.7 has been released with a new feature that detects outdated Secure Boot certificates, notifying users whose computers need updates before the older 2011-era Microsoft certificates expire in June 2026. The release also fixes a security issue where the /root folder was not properly restricted to the root user. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.6.2
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.6.2 is an emergency release addressing a critical sandbox escape vulnerability (CVE-2026-34078) in Flatpak 1.16.6. The flaw could allow an attacker who has already compromised Tor Browser to break its security confinement and access files in Persistent Storage. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.6.1
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.6.1 is an emergency release addressing important security vulnerabilities in Tor Browser. The update includes Tor Browser 15.0.9 (fixing several Firefox 140.9.1 vulnerabilities), Tor client 0.4.9.6, Thunderbird 140.9.0, and updated firmware packages for improved hardware support. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.6
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.6 introduces automatic Tor bridge discovery directly from the Tor Connection assistant, allowing users in censored regions to request region-appropriate bridges via the Moat API using domain fronting. The release also replaces KeePassXC with GNOME Secrets as the default password manager, offering better GNOME integration and accessibility while maintaining compatibility with existing KeePassXC databases. Additional updates include Electrum 4.7.0, Tor Browser 15.0.8, Thunderbird 140.8.0, and updated firmware packages. Several bug fixes address translation issues and automated upgrade problems.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.5
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.5 has been released with several updates: Tor Browser updated to 15.0.7, Tor client updated to 0.4.9.5, and Thunderbird updated to 140.7.1. A notable change is that Thunderbird can now be installed as additional software from Persistent Storage, ensuring users always have the latest version and avoiding the recurring issue of outdated Thunderbird builds with known security vulnerabilities. Mexican Spanish language pack support for Thunderbird is also added. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.4.2
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.4.2 is an emergency security release addressing critical Linux kernel vulnerabilities (DSA 6126-1) that could allow privilege escalation and potential deanonymization. The update patches the kernel to version 6.12.69, updates Thunderbird to 140.7.1, and fixes issues with Wi-Fi settings, Electrum reopening, and language persistence in the Welcome Screen.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.4.1
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.4.1 is an emergency security release addressing critical OpenSSL vulnerabilities that could potentially allow malicious Tor relays to deanonymize users. The update includes OpenSSL 3.5.4, Tor client 0.4.8.22, and Thunderbird 140.7.0. Additional fixes include Gmail authentication in Thunderbird and UI improvements for Wi-Fi settings. Automatic upgrades are available from Tails 7.0 or later.

recent_posts.title: Tails 7.4
recent_posts.summary: Tails 7.4 introduces persistent language and keyboard layout settings that save to USB stick for automatic application on restart. The release updates Tor Browser to 15.0.4, Thunderbird to 140.6.0, and Linux kernel to 6.12.63. BitTorrent download support has been dropped due to security concerns with v1 and migration costs to v2. Bug fixes include resolving GPG file opening in Kleopatra, desktop crashes with wrong VeraCrypt passwords, and inconsistent time format display.
